Quick technical note for Julie and the ClearMap team —

Summary recommendations (TL;DR):
- Default quantization: try 4-bit (QLoRA-style or hybrid INT4) for inference across the consumer-facing short prompt flows. Expect ~2.8x token cost reduction with minimal quality degradation on classification/short-generation tasks.
- Long-context summarization: keep at FP16/FP32 or 8-bit mixed precision for the heavy tails — quant can introduce hallucination risk when chaining many retrieval steps. We recommend an "escape hatch" where long summaries route to fp16 model variant.
- Batching guidance: use a short batching window (~15–30ms) for low-latency interactive traffic; for server-side bulk jobs (nightly re-runs) use larger batch sizes and longer windows to increase throughput.
- KV cache strategy: enable prefix caching for frequent retrieval hits. For your hit-rate estimates in the RFI the cache should reduce repeated token compute by ~20–30% during steady-state.

Operational constraints / caveats:
- Quantization reduces memory but can change model determinism—test your eval prompts under quantized weights.
- If you rely on LoRA-adapted weights for specialized prompts, validate LoRA compatibility with quantization path. We're happy to run a short eval pipeline with your sample prompts.

I can generate a small benchmark matrix (FP16 vs 8-bit vs 4-bit across 3 prompt classes) and attach numbers for the savings model.
